samples.summary: Per-occurrence `state.src.slice(state.pos, state.posMax)` is the one remaining super-linear-by-inspection step in the path this delta hardened, and it contradicts the file's own comment
samples.evidence: The delta removes the quadratic backtracking in IMG_TAG_RE, and the new comment (img-plugin.ts:53-62) asserts the tag match is "linear in the run of non-`<>` text". But every position where `startsImgTag` returns true still copies the remainder of the inline chunk at line 151 before the regex runs. `startsImgTag`'s own doc comment (lines 134-137) states the reason it exists is that "slicing the rest of the chunk each time would be quadratic in a long note" — yet the `<img`-prefix case does exactly that. Attack: a collaborator saves a note that is one paragraph of `"<img".repeat(25_000)` (100 KB). markdown-it treats `<` as a terminator char, so the inline ruler is invoked at each of the ~25k `<img` prefixes; the regex itself then fails in O(1) each time (the next char is `<`, which `\s` rejects), but each invocation first requests a ~50 KB-average substring. If the substring is materialised, that is ~2.5e9 char copies inside the synchronous `NotePreview.render()` (preview.ts:346) — the same stored, CRDT-shared main-thread hang the delta set out to remove. I could not complete the chain to an actual freeze: V8 (and JSC/SpiderMonkey) return a lazy SlicedString/dependent string for substrings this long, and irregexp consumes sliced strings with an offset without flattening, so on the browsers this ships to the slice is very likely O(1) and the input is harmless. Hence low confidence, but the code and its own comment disagree about whether that is being relied on. A `IMG_TAG_RE.lastIndex`-style sticky match (`/y` flag) against `state.src` directly would remove the ambiguity and the doubt.

finding.summary: Quadratic backtracking (ReDoS) in `IMG_TAG_RE` — a stored note can freeze every collaborator's preview
finding.evidence:
`const IMG_TAG_RE = /^<img(\s[^<>]*?)?\s*\/?>/i;` (img-plugin.ts:53) has two quantifiers that both match whitespace and are adjacent: the lazy `[^<>]*?` inside the optional group, and the greedy `\s*` that follows it. On an input that starts with `<img` and never closes, the engine tries every split of the whitespace run between the two quantifiers, and for each split backtracks `\s*` position by position looking for `>`; total work is O(n^2) in the length of the whitespace run.

Attack: a workspace member (notes are collaborative — see the stored-XSS SECURITY note at preview.ts:188) stores a note containing a single paragraph

    <img<SPACE repeated 200_000 times>x

(no `<` or `>` after it, and a trailing non-space so the paragraph trim does not remove the run). markdown-it's inline `text` rule treats `<` as a terminator, so `imgRule` runs at that position (img-plugin.ts:130), `startsImgTag` passes, and `IMG_TAG_RE.exec` at img-plugin.ts:132 enters ~2e10 backtracking steps on the main thread. `NotePreview.render()` calls `md.render()` synchronously into `this.el.innerHTML` (preview.ts:346) and is invoked on every document change, so the reader's tab hangs and — because the editor pane renders the same preview — is hard to recover from without deleting the note out of band.

This is not pre-existing behaviour: with `html: false` the `html_inline` rule is inert, and markdown-it's own `autolink` rule bails on this input after a single `indexOf('>')`. The new regex introduces the blowup. A possessive/atomic shape (e.g. dropping the inner `\s*` and letting `[^<>]*` be greedy, or requiring `>` via a cheap `indexOf` pre-check before running the regex) removes it.

verdict.reason: The quoted vulnerable regex is not in the repository. img-plugin.ts:64 defines IMG_TAG_RE as /^<img(\s[^<>]*)?>/i — a single greedy [^<>]* with nothing quantified after it and a mandatory literal '>' — not /^<img(\s[^<>]*?)?\s*\/?>/i as the finding claims. With only one quantifier over the attribute region there is no ambiguous split for the engine to backtrack over, so an unterminated '<img' followed by a long whitespace run is a single linear scan that fails at end-of-input. The doc comment at img-plugin.ts:53-62 explicitly names the exact pattern the finding quotes as the PRIOR shape and records that it was replaced because of this quadratic backtracking; the self-closing slash is handled separately by the linear SELF_CLOSE_RE (/\/\s*$/, img-plugin.ts:72, applied at :156). The remediation the finding proposes ("dropping the inner \s* and letting [^<>]* be greedy") is precisely what line 64 already implements. A regression test at img-plugin.test.ts:140-156 renders '<img' plus 100_000 spaces and asserts the render completes in under 1s, noting the old shape took ~11s. Repo-wide grep for the lazy class finds it only inside those two explanatory comments, and IMG_TAG_RE exists nowhere else. The finding's line numbers (53 for the regex, 130/132 for imgRule/exec vs. the real 64/148/151) are consistent with it having been written against a pre-fix revision.
